authorization: Authorize diagnosis and the small verified repairs, publication, and rechecks permitted by the selected CI module. Stop for repairs, decisions, or external blockers outside that module's automatic-remediation scope.

authorization: Authorize the complete release workflow for exactly the supplied repository and optional version under the selected modules: bounded release-preparation corrections, integration, tagging, and GitHub Release publication when permitted. Stop for decisions or blockers outside automatic scope; never bypass repository safeguards or alter unrelated work.

description: Analyze and implement one GitHub issue through bounded code changes pull request CI integration and verified issue resolution.

authorization: Authorize issue-scoped changes, pull-request and CI work, integration, and authority to close or verify automatic closure only after the owner workflow's resolution gate. authorization: Authorize synchronization of the selected work branch with its established base and publication when permitted by the selected integration module. Apply that module's history, conflict, verification, and protection rules; details such as when to prefer merge or rebase remain owned there. Never guess an ambiguous base; stop on semantic conflicts or unrelated work.

authorization: Read-only triage. Inspect only enough current remote evidence to prioritize actionable work and recommend the exact specialized command for each item when one exists. authorization: Perform evidence-led state-of-the-art analysis. Do not mutate repositories or permanent knowledge unless separately authorized.

authorization: Assess opportunities and evidence only. Do not claim guaranteed publication or return and do not mutate repositories unless separately authorized.

authorization: Authorize creation of the response-letter artifact required by the selected module. Do not claim unsupported changes or modify or publish the manuscript unless separately authorized.

When both repository and target journal are unambiguously supplied, authorize only the bounded local manuscript adaptation owned by papers/02_journal_adaptation.md, including required compilation and verification. Do not push, merge, submit, contact editors, make unrelated scientific changes, or infer an ambiguous mode.

While awaiting approval, a direct-continuation response consisting only of ok authorizes exactly the displayed revision batch within its approved PF items and acceptance criteria; code work may publish only to a safe work branch without merge. After batch completion, ok authorizes only the next batch proposal. Do not merge code branches, submit or contact the journal, broaden into unapproved items, or change the paper's central identity.

authorization: Read-only identity audit. Report confirmed files missing elements conflicts and pending decisions; do not modify or publish the repository.

In direct continuation, an isolated ok authorizes ChatGPT to apply, verify, and safely publish in-scope corrections through the shared remediation loop until the audit is clean, a human decision is required, a human checkpoint is prudent, or a concrete execution or verification step is better delegated to Codex. Any Codex handoff must be the minimum necessary next step, publish its verified state when safe, and return control to ChatGPT for independent review of the remote state and continued remediation. Do not exceed scope, protections, or stopping conditions.

description: Run a measured performance audit, report the prioritized optimization inventory, then on isolated ok enter a ChatGPT-first remediation loop that applies everything safely measurable and delegates only necessary benchmark or execution checkpoints to Codex.
scope: Exactly the supplied repository.
authorization: First invocation is inventory-only. In direct continuation, an isolated ok authorizes ChatGPT to apply, measure where its available execution surfaces permit, verify, and safely publish in-scope optimizations through the shared remediation loop. Delegate only the minimum benchmark, reproduction, fine-tuning, or other concrete execution step that requires Codex; review its published remote state and measurements for independent review before continuing. Do not exceed scope, protections, comparability requirements, or stopping conditions.

description: Run an evidence-led dead-code audit, report the prioritized inventory, then on isolated ok enter a ChatGPT-first remediation loop that removes or consolidates everything safely verifiable and delegates only concrete execution blockers to Codex.
scope: Exactly the supplied repository.
authorization: First invocation is inventory-only. In direct continuation, an isolated ok authorizes ChatGPT to apply, verify, and safely publish in-scope cleanup through the shared remediation loop until the audit is clean, a human decision is required, a human checkpoint is prudent, or a concrete execution or verification step is better delegated to Codex. Any Codex handoff must be minimal and return published state to ChatGPT for independent review of the remote state and continued remediation. Do not exceed scope, protections, removal-risk checks, or stopping conditions.

scope: Exactly the supplied repository and optional audit scope; when scope is omitted, inspect the repository's materially relevant automated-test surfaces without expanding into unrelated production work.
authorization: First invocation is inventory-only. Each direct-continuation ok authorizes exactly one bounded test-improvement batch defined by the selected workflow, with only its required verification and permitted publication. Do not exceed scope, protections, or stopping conditions.

authorization: Authorize bounded local reproduction work and, when materially useful, creation of the smallest focused regression test, reproduction harness, or fixture needed to demonstrate the supplied problem. Do not fix production behavior, do not broaden into a general bug audit, do not publish or mutate remote state, and do not claim reproduction without direct observed evidence.

A direct-continuation ok authorizes exactly the next remaining bounded batch from the already selected findings. Unresolved finding meaning, unrelated work, or work outside the delegated owner contract is not authorized.

authorization: Select the matching BUG or DEAD audit module from the code index and run the cyclic workflow with local fixes and verification. Never exceed ten correction batches. Preserve unrelated work and do not publish remotely unless separately authorized.

Preserve public contracts, observable behavior, relevant performance, unrelated work, and repository protections.
